9ag6v0vtlg8mqhgonhdd1h7ilv: An effect of our own. Ask has one operation, ask: it takes a question and gives back a Float64. It says nothing about where the answer comes from; whoever handles it decides.
e2528ifmt1rbq4kg1176s7d4gr: Asks twice and multiplies. Its type, () -[Ask]-> Float64, says it needs someone to answer Ask before it can run.
q96mq0eg9ue7p4oqrf7orptm3f: Abort, from the standard library: sharing among nobody stops with a reason instead of dividing by zero. Its type says it might abort.
7qsv6i9nll42fpdckdrqu0rf93: Two handlers. The first answers each ask (30 for the width, 12 otherwise), so area gives 360. The second turns an abort into a message. Each handler is a match whose arms are the effect's operations; once both are handled, main needs nothing but Console. Written in the editor with clicks only.

Influence: algebraic effects and handlers (Plotkin and Pretnar, 2009; the Eff language by Bauer and Pretnar), and effect rows in types as in Koka (Daan Leijen, 2014): https://koka-lang.github.io
Adapted: a handler is a match whose cases are the effect's operations, as OCaml 5.3 writes effect cases in match.
